passage: The corridor was crowded because rain kept everyone indoors, and children queued for the toilets. Vandana shoved a small boy out of the way and marched to the front. "I go first," she said, and her chest felt big and strong. Madhuri, the teacher, took her hand and stepped aside. "Pushing stops here. I won't let anyone be pushed." Vandana's chin wobbled. "My cousin does it," she muttered. Madhuri said gently, "You can be strong by being my line leader, holding the door." Vandana looked at her, then at the door, and slowly nodded.

qa.q: Why were the children crowded in the corridor?
qa.a: Rain kept everyone indoors, so children queued for the toilets.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling when she pushed the small boy, and what might be under it?
qa.a: Vandana felt big and strong, but her wobbling chin suggests she may also feel sad or unsure. She says her cousin does it, so she may be copying someone.

qa.q: How did Madhuri set a firm limit and still stay warm?
qa.a: Madhuri said clearly that pushing stops and no one will be pushed. Then she offered another way to feel strong, as line leader holding the door.

qa.q: What might the small boy have felt when he was shoved?
qa.a: The small boy was probably startled and maybe frightened, since he was smaller. He would want a teacher to stop the pushing and keep the line fair.

grounding: A child pushes smaller children to feel powerful, and a teacher sets a firm limit warmly and offers another way to feel strong, without only punishing.
